subject: kissing bug
title: This Bug Bites Your Face While You Sleep. The Bite Isn't the Danger

scenes.text: This bug bites people on the face at night. The bite isn't what makes you sick.
It's called the kissing bug, because it often feeds around your lips and eyes while you sleep.
It drinks your blood for several minutes, and you barely feel it.
The danger comes after: while it feeds, it poops next to the bite.
Rub that in by scratching, and a parasite enters. About eight million people carry it.
So the kiss is harmless. What it leaves behind isn't.

description:
Kissing bugs bite around the mouth and eyes at night, but the parasite that causes Chagas disease is in their droppings, not their bite.
Scratching rubs infected feces into the wound or eyes; about 8 million people live with Chagas worldwide, and the bugs have been found in 32 US states.
Had you heard of the kissing bug before?
